title: Hourly to Annual Pay: Use Our Salary Sacrifice Mortgage Calculator to Understand Your Take-Home Pay
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual salary using 38-hour weeks. Estimate tax, Medicare, and super. See how a salary sacrifice mortgage calculator can help with home loan planning.
salarySummary: For a standard 38-hour week, annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 then by 52, before tax, Medicare, and super.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before deductions. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly figure accordingly. Remember that this calculation assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for entitlements like paid leave. For example, if the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, a casual employee receives $33.05 per hour (including loading). When using a calculator, never type a rate that already includes casual loading; instead, enter the base rate and select the casual loading option if applicable.

faqs.q: How can a salary sacrifice mortgage calculator help me?
faqs.a: A salary sacrifice mortgage calculator estimates how much you could save on tax by directing part of your pre-tax salary into your home loan. This reduces your taxable income, potentially lowering your tax bill while building equity faster. It works best when combined with your annual pay estimate to see the net effect on take-home pay and mortgage repayments.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert Hourly to Annual Pay

If you earn an hourly wage or have been offered a salary, understanding the annual equivalent is essential for budgeting, comparing job offers, and planning tax. The standard formula is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks.

For most full-time employees, a 38-hour week is the benchmark used by the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Australian Bureau of Statistics. Using this assumption, annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, if your hourly rate is $30.00, your annual salary would be $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280.

If you work part-time or casual hours, adjust the weekly figure. A fortnightly amount is simply the weekly figure multiplied by two, which can be useful for comparing with pay cycles.

### Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement. Many industries have award rates that are higher. The Fair Work Commission sets these rates, and they vary by occupation and experience level. Always check the relevant award for your job.

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate. For the minimum wage, that means $33.05 per hour. When using [the timesheet](/) on this site, enter your base hourly rate and tick the casual loading checkbox if applicable. Do not enter a rate that already includes loading.

### Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Employers must pay super guarantee contributions of 12% of your ordinary earnings, on top of your salary. This is not deducted from your pay. For the 2026–27 year, the maximum contribution base is $270,830. If your annual salary exceeds that, super is only paid on the first $270,830. Use our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) guide to see how salary sacrifice can affect your super.

## Estimating Tax and Medicare

Once you have your annual gross figure, you can estimate the tax you will pay using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

In addition, most residents pay a Medicare levy of 2% of taxable income. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed in this estimate. If your income is below a certain level, the levy may be reduced or waived.

For example, an annual salary of $80,000 would have tax calculated as:
- $0 on first $18,200
- 15% on $26,800 ($45,000 – $18,200) = $4,020
- 30% on $35,000 ($80,000 – $45,000) = $10,500
- Total tax = $14,520
- Medicare levy (2%) = $1,600
- Total deductions = $16,120
- Estimated take-home pay = $63,880

This is a simplified estimate. It does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. For a more detailed breakdown, see our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page.

### Using a Salary Sacrifice Mortgage Calculator

Salary sacrifice allows you to direct pre-tax income towards certain benefits, such as additional super contributions or a mortgage. A **salary sacrifice mortgage calculator** helps you see how much tax you could save by reducing your taxable income through mortgage payments. For example, if you sacrifice $10,000 of your salary into your home loan, your taxable income drops by $10,000, potentially saving you $3,000 to $4,500 in tax depending on your bracket.

This strategy can be particularly effective for homeowners looking to pay off their loan faster while lowering their annual tax bill. Our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains how salary packaging works with mortgages and other benefits.

## Average Earnings for Context

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time as $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). That equates to an annual salary of about $108,352. All employees total earnings average $1,579.20 per week, which includes part-time workers. These are averages, not medians for any specific job. Your actual pay may differ based on your industry, experience, and location.

## Important Disclaimer

Annual pay shown here is an estimate based on hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For a quick conversion, use [the timesheet](/) on our home page. For more detailed guides, visit our [reference tables](/data) or [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page.
